alignments.note: Hortatory subjunctive with its auxiliary let and subject us; after is the English verb's own particle, no preverb or preposition answering to it (rules 9, 106).
Substantival article takes the supplied nominal and, its modifier being a verbless genitive, the supplied relativizer as well; head on the nominal word (rules 22, 31).
Inner article with no English determiner (rule 23).

The supplied lexical verb and its preposition ride with the noun the clause predicates, no preposition or determiner-bearing article standing to carry them (rules 62, 67). Placing make for on the article τῆς remains defensible.
Substantival article takes the supplied nominal things (rule 22).
Inner article with no English determiner.
οἰκοδομῆς recast as a finite clause; the supplied subject and modal are its helpers and head is the lexical verb (rules 7, 9, 17).

The second attributive article carries the relativizer of its verbless prepositional modifier (rule 31) and εἰς is spelled into the -by of the portmanteau, so both tokens take the single word as one aligned unit headed on the pronominal element (rule 35).
Reciprocal ἀλλήλους → one another, headed on the ἄλλος-word (rule 83).

whereby is taken as realizing the second article's relativizer together with εἰς rather than leaving the preposition unrepresented (rules 35, 36).
